meta.title: Who wrote "A Whiter Shade of Pale"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: The authorship was fought in court for years. Credited to Gary Brooker and Keith Reid, Procol Harum's 1967 hit was ruled in 2009 to be co-written by organist Matthew Fisher. What the courts actually decided.
meta.ogTitle: Who wrote 'A Whiter Shade of Pale'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Brooker and Reid — but in 2009 the House of Lords ruled organist Matthew Fisher a co-author of the music. A rare case of authorship settled by a court.

writing.label: Credited to Brooker & Reid — Matthew Fisher ruled a co-author in 2009
writing.sourceLine: For decades Procol Harum’s 1967 hit was credited to Gary Brooker (music) and Keith Reid (lyrics). Then the band’s original organist, Matthew Fisher, sued for a share of the authorship of its famous organ melody — and, after a four-year case, the UK’s highest court agreed.
writing.writer: Gary Brooker and Keith Reid, with Matthew Fisher (co-author, established 2009)
writing.definitiveVersion: Procol Harum’s 1967 recording — a UK No. 1 and one of the best-selling singles of the era.
trail: Matthew Fisher, Procol Harum’s organist, launched legal action in 2005, claiming he composed the song’s Bach-influenced organ melody. Brooker and Reid contested it, saying the song was written before Fisher joined.

In December 2006 the High Court ruled Fisher was a co-author of the music and awarded him a share of future royalties. The Court of Appeal agreed he was a co-author but held he had waited too long to claim, and awarded nothing.

In July 2009 the House of Lords — one of its final rulings before becoming the UK Supreme Court — restored Fisher’s status as co-author, entitling him to a share of royalties from then on. His authorship of the organ line is now legally established; the original Brooker–Reid credit stands alongside it.

context.heading: Why authorship was genuinely unclear
lead: This is not a case of the public crediting the wrong person — it is one where the writers themselves disagreed, and the answer had to be settled in court. Both sides had a real claim: Brooker and Reid wrote the song’s structure and words; Fisher shaped the organ melody that much of the record’s identity rests on.

We report the outcome rather than take a side: the courts found Fisher a co-author of the music, while leaving the original credit to Brooker and Reid in place. It stands as one of the few famous songs whose authorship carries a documented legal ruling.
context.pull: One of the few hit songs whose authorship was decided by a nation's highest court.
